# The Perses dashboards generated by diagram-kit's perses-dashboard, with no fixer of our own. CRC 4.22.7, COO 1.5.3,
# Option C (chart ipsec-nas-option-c-metrics deployed by Argo CD, pod ipsec-nas-metrics-tcmr8), 2026-10-07 13:50-14:20Z.
# diagram-kit 0.2.1 (https://github.com/ephico2real2/diagram-kit, tag v0.2.1), percli 0.54.0 from
# docker.io/persesdev/perses:v0.54.0 on podman.

## 1. Before: the kit refused the Grafana file
  $ perses-dashboard charts/ipsec-nas-option-c-metrics/files/ipsec-nas-option-c.json out.json --datasource ipsec-nas-thanos   (kit 0.2.0)
  perses-dashboard: the legend ['{{node}}: {{version}}'] of 'libreswan version per node' names several labels, and a
  Perses StatChart shows one (percli wrote metricLabel 'node}}: {{version'): give it one label in the Grafana source
  With kit 0.2.1 (a legend of two labels is the series name and the label shown; "suffix: days" is the unit days) the
  unchanged Grafana file converted, 23 panels. Against the committed Perses file (scripts/perses-dashboard-fix.py's),
  compared panel by panel, it differed in exactly this: the per-node table still had its 11 queries, the panel
  nas_identity was missing, and 13 coloured table cells had textColor #000000. The two stats and the two panels
  counting days were equal.

## 2. The change to charts/ipsec-nas/files/ipsec-nas.json (the only file edited)
  Per node (id 14): queries A (by node, pod) and K (by node, peer_id) removed; the nine left renamed A to I; the
    organize transformation and the overrides follow.
  NAS identity per node (id 30, new, under it, h 5): one query,
    max by (node, pod, peer_id) (ipsec_nas_tunnel_info{node=~"$node"}) or on (node, pod) max by (node, pod) (ipsec_nas_collect_timestamp_seconds{node=~"$node"})
    Every panel below moves down by 5.
  The query through Thanos Querier, $node = .*:
    as written:                              {node="crc", pod="ipsec-nas-metrics-tcmr8", peer_id="O=KCS OpenShift lab, CN=crc-nas.lab.internal"}
    without the "or" clause:                 the same one series
    ipsec_nas_tunnel_info{node="no-such-node"} (no tunnel): {node="crc", pod="ipsec-nas-metrics-tcmr8"}
  So a node whose tunnel is down keeps its reporting pod, which Grafana's single table showed and the fixer's panel did not.

## 3. Regenerated: scripts/perses-dashboard.sh
  wrote charts/ipsec-nas/files/ipsec-nas.perses.json (24 panels)
  wrote charts/ipsec-nas-option-c-metrics/files/ipsec-nas-option-c.perses.json (24 panels)
  Run a second time (kit installed from the tag v0.2.1): the five generated files have the same sha256.
  Against the Perses files committed before, panel by panel (by section, title and kind): the same 24 panels. Different:
    - 13 coloured table cells have textColor #000000 (Per node 10, Pods using NAS claims 3);
    - the descriptions of Per node and NAS identity per node, and the identity query's "or" clause (section 2);
    - the y of the panels in History and Storage on the NAS, +5 (each section is a grid of its own: no visible change);
    - the identity panel's key, 3_1 where the fixer named it nas_identity, and the order of its two hidden columns.
  tests/test-chart.sh 17 ok, tests/test-option-c-chart.sh 40 ok, tests/test-shared-collector.sh 8 ok,
  tests/test-metrics-collector.sh 37 ok, tests/test-doc-links.sh and tests/test-alert-rules.sh exit 0.

  The new Option C dashboard was applied as a second PersesDashboard (ipsec-nas-kit-check) beside the deployed one, and
  developer was given view, persesdashboard-viewer-role and persesdatasource-viewer-role in kcs-ipsec; all removed
  afterwards. The deployed dashboard's spec.config had the same sha256 before and after.
    deployed (before): 6 sections; Per node: crc UP YES PRESENT YES YES 3 7.92 requests/sec 0 2.68d;
                       NAS identity per node: crc ipsec-nas-metrics-tcmr8 O=KCS OpenShift lab, CN=crc-nas.lab.internal
    generated by the kit: the same rows; libreswan version per node 5.3; Certificate source per node C; Soonest
                       certificate expiry 2.0 years; no NaN, no Forbidden; "No data" only on Kernel IPsec errors per node
    cell text on #73bf69, dark theme: before rgb(255,255,255), 2.24 to 1; after rgb(0,0,0), 9.39 to 1
  Forced cases (a query changed in a copy of the dashboard):
    IKE SA query with node="no-such-node": the IKE SA cell is empty, the row stays one row
    identity query with ipsec_nas_tunnel_info{node="no-such-node"}: crc | ipsec-nas-metrics-tcmr8 | (empty)

## 6. Later that day (15:10-15:20Z): the Per node table fills its panel in Grafana
  After section 2 every column of Per node had a width (170 + 940 px), and in Grafana the table ended at about three
  quarters of its panel: before, the NAS identity column, which has none, took the rest. The width of Node is removed
  from the Grafana file; the only change in the Perses files is that the column "node" has no "width".
  Grafana 12.3.1 (as section 5): 33 queries, failed 0, no series 1; the table spans the panel, Node the widest column.
  Console (as section 4): the same row, crc UP YES PRESENT YES YES 3 8.21 requests/sec 0 2.73d; the columns are
  spread as before (Perses spreads them either way).
  The four captures of sections 4 and 5 were taken again with this change and replace the earlier ones.

## 7. The review after the merge (2026-10-07), and what it changed
  The change of sections 1 to 5 was merged without a review. One ran afterwards, read-only, with the real percli
  0.54.0, the Perses 0.54.0 UI and promtool. Of its ten claims about the kit change and this repository:
    confirmed: the two stats and the unit days as the fixer wrote them; the nine queries of Per node, their
      columns and overrides; the identity query (promtool: tunnel up, no tunnel info, two pods with one or both
      reporting a tunnel, an empty identity); the grid (30 panels, 1728 of 1728 cells, 0 overlapping);
      the counts 24, 33 and 13; the contrast 2.24 and 9.39.
    refuted or incomplete, all corrected:
      - scripts/perses-dashboard.sh wrote its five files one by one. With Option C's conversion failing after
        Option B's, four files were new and Option C's Perses file old, and both chart tests passed in that state;
        with scripts/option-c-dashboard.py refusing the source, an empty ipsec-nas-option-c.json.tmp was left.
        Now all five are made as <target>.tmp and moved together at the end; tests/test-perses-dashboard-script.sh.
        On the script as merged: 2 ok, 3 FAIL. On the corrected one: 5 ok.
      - PERSES_DASHBOARD=perses-dashboard (a name on the PATH, not a path) was "not found". Now found.
      - doc 61 said the fixer "rewrote four panels": five, and it added a sixth.
      - doc 61 said a failed check "says which panel": true where a panel is at fault.
      - doc 61's table of differences lacked IPsec drops (1h): red and without decimals in Grafana above zero,
        the plain number in Perses (forced to 1.0169 on the lab's data by the review, in the Perses UI).
      - the kit itself (0.2.1) wrote out a label percli broke without a brace ("{{ node }}", a fixed text) and
        lost a unit without a word when a panel sets no decimals; neither occurs in this dashboard. Kit 0.2.2.
  Regenerated with kit 0.2.2 and the corrected script: the five files have the same sha256 as before.
